original_question: When a feedback controller acts continuously, meaning that its actuation period is shorter than every characteristic time scale of the system dynamics, how can the results obtained for discrete repeated feedback actuation be extended to this continuous-time limit despite the nontrivial relation between discrete entropy and differential entropy?
target_in_paper: Section III.1.2 “Continuous Actuation of the Feedback Controller”
correct_elements: It correctly captures (1) the definition of continuous actuation as actuation period shorter than any characteristic system time scale, (2) the goal of extending the discrete repeated-actuation results to the continuous-time limit, and (3) the obstruction posed by the nontrivial relation between discrete Shannon entropy and continuous differential entropy.
missing_details: Precise statement of the discrete repeated-actuation result to be extended (the average entropy reduction formula ΔS=–∑I(X_k;C_k|C^{k–1}) from Cao & Feito 2009),
Definition of the random variables: system macrostate X_k, control action C_k, and control history C^{k–1},
Specification that the discrete result refers to correlated repeated actuations (Section II.4, Eq. (15)),
Explicit mention of the limit τ→0 of the actuation period τ,
Clarification that differential entropy h(·) replaces discrete H(·) in continuous time and that one seeks an entropy rate formulation,
Assumption on system evolution between actuations and existence of well‐defined entropy rate in the limit
Reference to Cover & Thomas 1991 [18] for the discrete–differential entropy relation
refined_question: Consider a physical system whose state X(t) evolves continuously under dynamics with characteristic time scales τ_c, and a feedback controller that measures the system and applies control actions C_k at discrete times t_k=kτ. Cao and Feito (2009) showed that for correlated repeated discrete actuations the total average entropy reduction of the system is ΔS_discrete=–∑_{k=1}^N I(X_k;C_k|C^{k–1}) (Section II.4, Eq. (15)). In the limit of continuous actuation τ→0 (τ≪τ_c), how can one rigorously derive the corresponding continuous-time entropy reduction rate in terms of differential entropy and mutual information rates, accounting for the nontrivial relationship between discrete Shannon entropies H(·) and continuous differential entropies h(·)?
justification: The draft question corresponds directly to the open problem stated in Section III.1.2, but omits key definitions and references needed to make it self-contained and faithful to the paper. We have specified the discrete result (Eq. (15) in Section II.4), defined the relevant random variables, introduced the limit τ→0, and clarified the role of differential versus discrete entropy. This aligns precisely with the paper’s intent without broadening or altering the problem.
